text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Models train on April 2024–June 2025; their forecasts are scored July 2025–June 2026 (Fold A). Both panels score forecasts for the same meters at the same times; each panel has its own scale. Panel 1 keeps production training settings and changes wind and radiation processing together. Panel 2 keeps corrected inputs and changes the training recipe. Each weather member is an alternative weather forecast. Production training predicts one power value per weather member with one forecasting model per meter. A quantile is a threshold below which a specified fraction of outcomes should fall. Quick-wins training predicts nine values at specified probabilities, called quantiles. Quick-wins shares one forecasting model across meters of each type and changes its inputs and their preparation. Panel 2 measures those recipe changes together; it does not isolate quantile training. Primary training settings; robustness checks are reported separately. Predictions near to and far from issuance are combined. Three training runs use different random choices during training. A seed sets those choices. Forecasts describe possible power outputs and their probabilities. Loss scores those predicted probabilities against observed power. Pinball loss penalises predicted quantiles that fall above or below observed power. Production delivers 51 power predictions; quick-wins pools nine quantiles per weather forecast into 459 values. Each recipe's values are sorted and given equal weight. Each scoring probability selects the first sorted value whose cumulative fraction reaches that probability. The common score is twice the mean pinball loss at 19 probabilities for each issued distribution. Reported mean differences give each meter and each of the three training runs equal weight. To assess variation, we recompute the average loss difference using all forecasts and observations in a selection of whole months. Recalculations repeatedly select whole months and a seed shared by both forecasts. Months can be selected more than once in a recalculation. The line covers the middle 95% of the resulting loss differences. “All series” averages all 31 metered series, including demand, solar, wind, biofuel, and battery storage. Loss differences are percentage points of each meter's frozen capacity. Capacity is a fixed power scale: the 99th percentile of each meter's absolute power readings. The scale uses the full available history, including readings after the scored period. Dot: mean loss difference on matched forecasts. Line: 95% interval from repeated draws of whole months and one matched training seed. Negative loss differences favour the forecast named before minus in each panel. All rows are planned: written into the study plan before any result existed.'
text.tspan: Models train on April 2024–June 2025; their forecasts are scored July 2025–June 2026 (Fold A).
Both panels score forecasts for the same meters at the same times; each panel has its own scale.
Panel 1 keeps production training settings and changes wind and radiation processing together.
Panel 2 keeps corrected inputs and changes the training recipe.
Each weather member is an alternative weather forecast.
Production training predicts one power value per weather member with one forecasting model per meter.
A quantile is a threshold below which a specified fraction of outcomes should fall.
Quick-wins training predicts nine values at specified probabilities, called quantiles.
Quick-wins shares one forecasting model across meters of each type and changes its inputs and their preparation.
Panel 2 measures those recipe changes together; it does not isolate quantile training.
Primary training settings; robustness checks are reported separately.
Predictions near to and far from issuance are combined.
Three training runs use different random choices during training.
A seed sets those choices.
Forecasts describe possible power outputs and their probabilities.
Loss scores those predicted probabilities against observed power.
Pinball loss penalises predicted quantiles that fall above or below observed power.
Production delivers 51 power predictions; quick-wins pools nine quantiles per weather forecast into 459 values.
Each recipe's values are sorted and given equal weight.
Each scoring probability selects the first sorted value whose cumulative fraction reaches that probability.
The common score is twice the mean pinball loss at 19 probabilities for each issued distribution.
Reported mean differences give each meter and each of the three training runs equal weight.
To assess variation, we recompute the average loss difference using all forecasts and observations in a selection
of whole months.
Recalculations repeatedly select whole months and a seed shared by both forecasts.
Months can be selected more than once in a recalculation.
The line covers the middle 95% of the resulting loss differences.
“All series” averages all 31 metered series, including demand, solar, wind, biofuel, and battery storage.
Loss differences are percentage points of each meter's frozen capacity.
Capacity is a fixed power scale: the 99th percentile of each meter's absolute power readings.
The scale uses the full available history, including readings after the scored period.
Dot: mean loss difference on matched forecasts. Line: 95% interval from repeated draws of whole months and one
matched training seed.
Negative loss differences favour the forecast named before minus in each panel.
All rows are planned: written into the study plan before any result existed.
